item.content:encoded: I would like to see some anomalous behaviour in the actual game. Perhaps, in order for the video to respond to a participant's answers, they have to have claimed a game piece and are attempting to move it around the board. Like everything those weird late 80's/early 90's VHS board games wish they could be. As it stands, it's strange that the game has the primary SCP designation when it just appears to be a delivery mechanism for the VHS.

The contestants, host, and audience will have no visible reaction to profanity, vulgarity, or racial slurs given as an answer.

The contestants, host, and/or audience did have visible reactions to profanity, vulgarity, or racial slurs as an answer. Maybe reactions specially gauged based upon the content of questions—like, if the questions are racially offensive, racial slurs would be met with laughter and/or applause, if questions are absurd and sexual, then absurd sexual jokes be met with mixed laughter and groans of disgust.

item.content:encoded:
Okay, I decided to upvote after it turned out that everyone in the audience is somebody who's watched/is watching the tape. Nice little implying twist there.

But Bright and yoric are semi-right, while I don't think it's "meh" enough to warrant a downvote/neutral vote, it is "meh" in a couple areas. It's like you've made a very good skeleton and put a couple bits of flesh on, but nothing really more. In this case I'm really not sure whether or not putting in experiment logs and the like would do anything if they didn't add anything more. Defer to those older and wiser than me.
